newsitem.title: UK: British inflation rises to 2.6 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: British inflation rises to 2.6 pct in May.

text.p: Britain's annual inflation rate rose to 2.6 percent in May from 2.4 percent in April, official figures showed on Thursday.
The Office of National Statistics said the rise was mainly due to an increase in housing costs.
The government's target rate, which excludes mortgage costs, held steady at 2.5 percent, meaning the incoming Labour administration has hit the target in its first full month in office.
The inflation rate rose by 0.4 percent in May after a monthly rise of 0.6 percent in April.
Analysts said the figures gave some cause for concern.
Philip Shaw of Union Plc said: "The numbers are a little disappointing given hopes that sterling's strength would lead to a further decline in underlying inflation."
